strings.name: Craig Jelinek
strings.summary: Craig Jelinek is an American retail executive who rose from warehouse operations to Costco's top management, serving as CEO from 2012 until handing over to Ron Vachris in January 2024. He continued its low-price membership model and emphasized employee pay and retention in public testimony; he did not found Costco.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026; recent personal activity is supported by his university's March 12 report on entrepreneurial mentoring. CEO, president, employee and director tenures are distinguished; historical wage announcements are not current pay standards.
strings.influence.rationale: Led Costco over many years, advancing the expansion and operating culture of membership warehouse retail.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: A 1975 business administration alumnus of San Diego State University; secondary summaries are not used to infer two separate degrees.
strings.facts.f2.label: President and CEO tenures
strings.facts.f2.value: He was president and CEO from January 2012 to February 2022, then remained CEO through the end of 2023; the presidency had already passed to Vachris.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Membership business model
strings.highlights.h1.text: Limited product selection, high sales volume and simple warehouses helped control costs and offer members low prices; he continued an existing company model rather than inventing it alone.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Employees and business performance
strings.highlights.h2.text: His 2021 Senate testimony connected pay and benefits with employee retention; these statements express the company's business position, not an independent assessment of all working conditions.
strings.timeline.t1.title: University reports on mentoring
strings.timeline.t1.text: SDSU reported his advice to student entrepreneur Sandy Basaka; they first met in November 2024, not on the article's publication date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Leaves Costco's board
strings.timeline.t2.text: A later company proxy statement confirmed the month of his board retirement, separate from his earlier CEO and employee retirements.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Ends transitional employment
strings.timeline.t3.text: After advising his successor through the transition, he retired as an employee; his board service had not yet ended.
strings.timeline.t4.title: CEO handover takes effect
strings.timeline.t4.text: Ron Vachris became president and CEO, while Jelinek temporarily retained advisory and director roles.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Submits Senate testimony
strings.timeline.t5.text: He said the starting wage in US stores would rise to $16 an hour the following week; this was company starting-pay policy, not average pay or national minimum-wage legislation.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes Costco CEO
strings.timeline.t6.text: He succeeded Jim Sinegal; the appointment had been announced in August 2011.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becomes president and COO
strings.timeline.t7.text: He took on broader operating responsibilities and worked with Sinegal to prepare the leadership transition.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins Costco
strings.timeline.t8.text: He began as a warehouse manager and later held operations and merchandising roles; the year follows company and university sources.
